title: Water tank temperature sensor open
shortDescription: Brondell Swash CL series detects open thermistor on storage tank.
fullDescription: Brondell Swash CL1500 and CL1700 use a heated water reservoir. E1 indicates the controller cannot read the tank thermistor - usually a connector that shook loose during shipping or after cleaning the seat.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug seat for 5 minutes and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Warranty
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, contact Brondell - the seat is a sealed unit.

faq.a: Yes temporarily, but heater stays disabled.

title: Heater dry-fire prevention
shortDescription: Tank water level sensor reports empty during heating cycle.
fullDescription: Brondell's heater includes a low-water cutoff. E2 means the float reads empty even though water is supplied - common after the inlet filter clogs or after a long power outage drained the tank.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet filter
fixSteps.instruction: Shut water, disconnect supply, rinse the screen at the seat inlet.

title: Wand position error
shortDescription: Spray wand encoder out of range.
fullDescription: The wand drive uses an optical encoder. E3 fires when the wand fails to home or extend within the timeout window - usually due to scale buildup on the rails.

fixSteps.title: Self-clean
fixSteps.instruction: Press WAND CLEAN to flush the wand.

fixSteps.title: Vinegar wipe
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe wand with white vinegar, rinse, retest.

title: Seat sensor not detected
fullDescription: Wash will not engage unless the seat senses an occupant. E4 typically follows a deep clean where moisture seeped into the sensor pad on the underside of the seat.

fixSteps.title: Dry sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Lift seat and dry the underside.

faq.a: Lock the seat in standby with the side panel.

title: Heater overtemperature
fullDescription: The reservoir heater has a 100C thermal fuse. E5 means the cutoff opened - typically from heavy scale insulating the element. The heater module must be replaced.

fixSteps.title: Stop and unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug immediately and contact Brondell support.

title: Dryer heater fault
shortDescription: Air-dry heating element open or shorted.
fullDescription: The dryer's PTC heating element is monitored for resistance. E6 fires when readings fall outside the expected range - usually because the element burned out from prolonged use without airflow.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum intake
fixSteps.instruction: Clear the rear intake grille with a vacuum.

faq.a: Standard cycle is 3 minutes - extend with the timer button.

title: Deodorizer fan stalled
shortDescription: Carbon deodorizer fan tach out of range.
fullDescription: The deodorizer module pulls bowl air through a carbon filter. E7 means the small fan stopped spinning - usually because the carbon cartridge was reinstalled incorrectly and is jamming the impeller.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the carbon cartridge and reinsert with the arrow up.

title: Remote signal lost
shortDescription: RF remote not pairing with seat.
fullDescription: Brondell's wireless remote runs at 2.4 GHz on later models. E8 means pairing was lost - typically after battery replacement or after a router on the same band saturates the channel.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the seat's PAIR button 5 seconds and press any remote button.

faq.a: Yes - the side panel is hard-wired.

title: Drip at supply T
fullDescription: After installation a small drip can appear at the brass T-valve. Almost always caused by a missing or pinched rubber washer at the compression fitting. Do not over-tighten - replace the washer.

fixSteps.title: Replace washer
fixSteps.instruction: Shut water, disconnect, install new washer, hand-tight plus a quarter turn.

faq.a: Only on tank inlet threads, not compression nuts.

title: Seat dead - GFCI tripped
fullDescription: All Swash models plug into a GFCI outlet. Any moisture or surge will trip it. Press RESET on the receptacle - if it trips again immediately the seat or the cord may be faulted.

faq.a: Yes, but it must be GFCI-listed.
